text:
I compared this file against the known `ms@2.1.3` source line by line.

The only textual difference from the released 2.1.3 code is the added `case '':` inside the `minutes` branch of the `parse` switch. This case is unreachable, for two independent reasons:

1. The capture group `(match[2])` can only ever be a non-empty string (one of the unit alternatives, each of which requires at least one character) or `undefined` (when the optional group doesn't participate). It can never be the empty string.
2. Even if `match[2]` could be `''`, the line `var type = (match[2] || 'ms').toLowerCase();` coerces any falsy value to `'ms'` before the switch, so `type` could never equal `''` anyway.

Therefore the added case is dead code and cannot alter any observable behaviour — parsing, formatting, error throwing, and numeric edge cases all behave exactly as in 2.1.3. This is an equivalent refactor.

```json
{"defect": false, "note": "The only change from ms@2.1.3 is an added `case '':` in the minutes branch of parse(), which is unreachable: match[2] can never be an empty string, and even if it were, `(match[2] || 'ms')` would coerce it to 'ms' before the switch. The behaviour is identical to the released version."}
```
